as_told: At Interplay, producers always asked for at least one change. The artist who animated the queen in Battle Chess (1988) gave her a pet duck in every animation, kept clear of the real animation. At the review the producer watched it all and said: 'That looks great. Just one thing - get rid of the duck.'
lesson: Give a reviewer an obvious, harmless thing to remove so the work you care about is left alone.
what_happened: The earliest telling found is a Stack Overflow answer by the user 'kyoryu', dated about 14 March 2010, who calls it 'Interplay corporate lore' and says he did not originate the story. In 2016 a commenter signing as Bill Dugan, who said he was a junior employee at Interplay in 1989 (a Bill Dugan is credited on Interplay's 1989 Dragon Wars manual), wrote that the story is true except for details: lead Battle Chess artist Todd Camasta put a still image of a duck, not an animation, into the NES game Total Recall, and the approver 'supposedly' asked for it to be removed. No record from 1988-1990 was found. The account does not come from the artist or the approver, so the event itself is not shown by any record.

earliest_telling.where: Answer 'A Duck' to the question 'New programming jargon you coined?' (stackoverflow.com question 2349378, later deleted)
earliest_telling.quote: he gave the queen a pet duck

original.what: Comment on Jeff Atwood's 'New Programming Jargon' discussion (Coding Horror forum), posted under the name Bill Dugan, who says he worked at Interplay in 1989
original.quote: Todd Camasta (who had indeed been the lead artist for Battle Chess) put in the duck, but it was a still image, not animated, and it was in the NES game

original.what: Same Stack Overflow answer: the teller's statement that the story was received lore, not his own experience
original.quote: This started as a piece of Interplay corporate lore.

lesson_verdict.why: No study was found that tests whether a planted decoy flaw protects the rest of a piece of work in review. Parkinson's 'law of triviality' (1957), often linked to this story, is satire, not evidence.

confidence_note: The only account from someone at Interplay is the 2016 Dugan comment, written 27 years later by a person who was neither the artist nor the approver; its key line is 'supposedly', and his identity was not confirmed. If his account is right, the story is misattributed (Total Recall on NES, a still image). A VOGONS forum post reports an undocumented '/ducks' switch in the VGA Battle Chess program, which, if real, would point back to Battle Chess; it could not be checked. No lesson source was found, so the lesson source fields are empty.
